preamble: The shift from a voiceless palatal stop [c] to an alveolar sibilant [s] is a common path in the development of Romance languages, typically occurring through an intermediate affricate stage [ts]. In Panará (Jê) the Proto-Jê palatal stop *c became s, as in sy 'seed' and si 'bone'.

examples.note: Historical palatalization of Latin [k] before front vowels led to [c], then [ts], and finally [s] in French.

Panará devoiced and merged *c and *ĵ as s, directly from the Proto-Goyaz Jê palatal stop. Forms in Nikulin's Macro-Jê alphabet: c = voiceless palatal stop or coronal affricate, ĵ = its voiced counterpart, ñ = [ɲ], y = [ɨ ~ ɯ], ə̂ = [ɘ ~ ɤ], ô/ê = close-mid vowels.

Forms in Eddyshaw's transcription: j = [ɟ], y = [j], ɩ ʋ = [ɪ ʊ], a tilde below a vowel marks nasalization, ' marks a glottalized vowel; POV = Proto-Oti-Volta; the final syllable of nouns is a noun-class suffix. Nõotre (cà̰aná) and Buli (nícháanoā) keep the palatal stop.
Nõotre cètɔ́, Buli chōroā keep the stop.
Eddyshaw: apart from Nõotre, all Western Oti-Volta languages changed *c to s; Nawdm (sááná 'stranger', sídá 'husband') shares the change.
